- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.35) within last 3–5 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment unit.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends after strong upward moves; add 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment if prior 3–5 days show >+5% average gain.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply linear decay adjustment: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day from day 10 onward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.38, +0.68), model fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of 2–3 recent values for smoothing.
